title.narrative: Provision of emergency unconditional multi-purpose cash support for vulnerable communities in Jebel Saman, Aleppo governorate.

description.narrative: ltpgtFollowing 14 years of conflict, Syria is currently dealing with a range of complex compounding challenges and facing the highest level of humanitarian needs since the start of the crisis, and the situation continues to deteriorate (Syria Humanitarian Response Priorities Jan-Mar 2025, issued January 2025). The deteriorating economic situation has led to major gaps in the provision of basic needs for many Syrian families. In combination with the continued fluctuation of the Syrian pound, the sharp increase in prices and reduced income levels, affected populations are facing major financial challenges in accessing food items and other basic needs. The needs are especially high in Aleppo governorate, which has been highly impacted by the conflict and the 2023 earthquakes, leaving many residents without jobs and buildings and basic infrastructure damaged. With inter-sectoral severity scale 4, Jebel Saman subdistrict is one of the most vulnerable in Aleppo, with a total of 928,640 persons in need (56%) according to HNO/ UNOCHA data for 2024/25. ltbrgtTo further identify the needs and preferences of the community and assess the feasibility of CVA programming, ZOA conducted specific assessments for Jebel Saman subdistrict, including FGDs, KII, a rapid Market Assessment, and a Financial Service Providers Capacity Assessment (see uploaded reports with detailed findings). Based on these identified needs and confirmed feasibility of CVA programming, MPCA is selected as a preferred assistance modality. ltbrgtWith this project, ZOA will target 1150 vulnerable households in Jebel Saman subdistrict with unconditional multi-purpose cash support for three monthly rounds. The transfer value is aligned with the recommendation of the Cash Working Group (CWG) and is currently set at 100USD per month per household. ZOA’s market assessment in Jebel Saman subdistrict established the local market functionality and accessibility and confirmed the feasibility of the cash modality in this location (full market assessment report is uploaded).ltbrgtAfter a Financial Service providers mapping exercise and a capacity assessment checklist (see document uploaded), ZOA will work with Al Fouad as Financial Service provider to conduct the cash transfer distributions, using its existing framework agreement with this service provider. ZOA has a team of local and trained volunteers to conduct the distributions in an inclusive manner. ltbrgtDuring the distributions, ZOA will conduct During Distribution Monitoring (DDM) to receive immediate feedback on the approach, process, staff behavior, etc. Furthermore, ZOA will also conduct Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) to evaluate the impact of the assistance and gather information on the indicators included in the logframe. ltbrgtLastly, ZOA will also conduct regular market monitoring to assess the effects of the assistance on the local market and ensure that the project does not create negative impact.lt/pgt
